texts.facts: DAR was filed by MACT No. 882/2021 Vikas Vs. Shankar Yadav & Ors.
texts.arguments: . It is argued by Ld. Counsel for Insurance Company that footpath is not meant for sleeping thus the victims had actively contributed to the accident which has been squarely contested by counsel for claimant who argued that it is the duty of the State to ensure safe shelter Further, that the offending vehicle was supposed to move on the road rather it crashed through the grill on the pavement which itself shows the extent of recklessness of the part of driver of the offending vehicle. Therefore, the contention of Ld. Counsel for Insurance Company is rejected and this Tribunal does not hold that victim in any manner was guilty of contributory negligence.

6. From the pleadings of parties, following issues were framed vide order dated 13.05.2022:
1) Whether the injured suffered injury in a road traffic accident on 19.01.2020 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR 38R 6325

OPP. 
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom ?

12. On the basis of material on record, evidence adduced and arguments addressed, issue wise findings are as under :-
MACT No. 882/2021 Vikas Vs. Shankar Yadav & Ors. Page No. 5 of 24 ISSUE NO.1 1) Whether the injured suffered injury in a

It is well settled that the proceedings before the Claims Tribunal are in the nature of inquiry and the finding of rash and negligent driving by driver of the offending vehicle is to be returned only at the touch stone of preponderance of p
The factors noted above are sufficient to conclude that preponderance of probability is made out showing negligence of respondent no.1 in causing the accident.
14. Police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under Section 279/337/338/304A IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent no.1 in causing the accident.
The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal.

In National Insurance Co.
Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet under relevant section are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

15. It is also settled that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him as observed by Hon'ble High Court of India in the case of Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamle
These are four connected matters.
Three persons were injured in the accident while one person namely Lallan died.
Three persons who are injured are called Adhe, his wife Banpatiya and his minor son Vikas.
Adhe and Banpatiya were produced as petitioners witnesses in connected 3 matters being injured persons.

But in death case of Lallan, they were not produced as eye MACT No.
882/2021 Vikas Vs. Shankar Yadav & Ors.
Page No. 6 of 24 witness, however, it is not mentioned by the counsel that the testimony of injured persons be read in the death case as well being connected case pertaining to same accident.

However, as these 4 DARs are the result of the same accident and the injured persons have testified about the same in their own DAR matters, there is no reason why those testimonies should not be read as testimonies of eye witnesses in deat

Therefore, evidence of Adhe and Banpatiya with respect to the mode and manner of accident as eye witness to the accident being injured themselves is being read as part and parcel of this case of death of Lallan.

It is categorically testified that those three injured persons along with Lallan were resting on the footpath under the Modi Mill Flyover on 09.01.2020 when suddenly at about 12.30 AM, speeding offending vehicle crashed through the grill of
Aadhe and Banpatiya were cross examined by counsel for the insurance company in the other three matters wherein they called themselves as eye witness and as victims to the incident.
They also stated during cross examination that a car had also subsequently hit the truck from behind after the accident.
They also categorically attributed the entire negligence on the part of speeding offending vehicle.
18. FIR was registered and police recorded statement of other injured persons.
There are certain photographs filed on record as part of DAR which are Ex.PW1/6 to Ex.PW1/11, which are self evident of the reckless driving on the part of driver of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute with respect to the identification of the offending vehicle or that of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Offending vehicle was found at the spot by police whereas the charge MACT No. 882/2021 Vikas Vs.
Shankar Yadav & Ors.
Page No. 7 of 24 sheet shows that the driver had fled away from the spot and his identity was subsequently revealed by the owner when notice under Section 133 MV Act was served upon him.

PW-1 wife of the deceased, during cross examination by counsel for Insurance Company deposed that other three injured persons were her relatives and on the day of accident,
they came to meet her deceased husband and at the time of accident,
R-1 & 2 has chosen not to cross examine this witness.
All the injured persons have been consistent in their statement before the police as well as their testimonies before the court with respect to the details of the accident.
Despite detailed cross examination by counsel for insurance company, any contradiction or inconsistency could not be elicited from the testimony of the eye witnesses.
The testimony has been very natural and convincing and thus inspires confidence.
There is thus no reason with the court to doubt the credibility or reliability of the witness.
No witness has been produced on behalf of respondent to place any defence or to raise doubt over the veracity of the witness or the testimony itself.
The offending vehicle was being driven on a public way.
As such, rashness and negligence has not been defined in MACT but it entails its meaning from Sec. 279 IPC which penalises rash and negligent driving on a public way so as to endanger human life.
Rashness and negligence has to be understood in a contextual sense depending upon the facts of any case.
In simple terms, it would mean driving without due and reasonable care towards the traffic rules and towards the safety of fellow commuters plying on the said public way.
High speed without doubt is a testament to rash driving but is not the sole exclusive criteria to so determine.

In the instant case, it is evident from bare perusal of the Site Plan that the offending vehicle could not negotiate the turn under the Modi Mill Flyover on MACT No. 882/2021 Vikas Vs. Shankar Yadav & Ors.
Page No. 8 of 24 account of its high speed and therefore, went beyond the control of the driver to breach the road and crashed into and over the footpath crushing and injuring the pavement dwellers.
Such was the impact of the accident that a crane had to be called for removing wheels of the truck from the body of deceased Lallan.

The driver simply fled away from the spot without even caring to remove the wheels of the truck from the body of the person crushed under the wheels, what to talk of offering any help to the injured persons.
There is no other conclusion possible than the reckless and brazen driving on the part of driver of offending vehicle was responsible for killing one and causing injuries to three others.

5 Contributory negligence 19.

It is argued by Ld. Counsel for insurance company that the victims contributed to the accident by sleeping on the road pavements and therefore, contributory negligence on their part must be deducted from the compensation to be awarded to th
It is admitted that all the four victims were resting/ sleeping on the pavement while Lallan used to reside their in a juggi, other three had come from native village to pay him a visit.
However, this Court cannot comment on the reason why those people were compelled to spend their nights on the pavement and why they could not afford to have some other suitable safe place to live.
It can least be called to be unfortunate that they were compelled to be out in open on a presumably chilly January night in the National Capital.
Least this Court can do is not to punish them for their helplessness which primarily made them victim of this extremely unfortunate incident.
No doubt a duty of reasonable care is inherent in every living being but their might be overwhelming compulsions pushing the person to compromise on the said duty in a bare bid to survive.

The victim must not be doubly punished for what they had to go MACT No. 882/2021 Vikas Vs. Shankar Yadav & Ors. Page No. 9 of 24 through or what they had to lose in the accident.
21.

22. As such, in view of the evidence proved on record and charge-sheet against R-1 and that R-1 did not appear in the witness box to deny the rash and negligence on the part of driver, in backdrop of the discussion made above, nothing remai
The contention of contributory negligence raised by counsel for insurance company stand rejected in terms of discussion made above.
It is held that rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle was responsible for causing death of Lallan and injuries to the other three.
Issue No.1 is decided accordingly, in favour of the petitioner and against respondent.

24. Before putting in frame the position of law, it is noted that the process of determining the compensation by the court is essentially a very difficult task and can never be an exact science.
Perfect compensation is hardly possible, more so in claims of injury and disability.

These general principles have been stated and reiterated in several decisions.
